**1 — Scene:** A breakfast tray with toast topped with a fried egg, avocado and a lemon wedge; a separate bowl of strawberries; Greek yogurt; and water.

**2 — Vessels:** The toast plate appears approximately **23 cm** across: area ≈ **415 cm²**. The strawberry bowl is approximately **20 cm** across: area ≈ **314 cm²**. I include both dishes and the yogurt as parts of the visible meal.

**3 — Items:** Toast, fried egg, avocado, lemon wedge, sliced strawberries, and Greek yogurt. No separately measurable oil or sauce is visible. Water contributes no energy and is excluded from food weight.

**4–6 — Area, volume, and weight:** Percentages below use non-overlapping visible footprints. For the toast, the effective height also accounts for bread underneath the egg.

| Item | Vessel area covered | Area × effective height = volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Toast | 26% of plate | 108 × 2.3 = 248 ml | 0.30 g/ml | 74 g |
| Fried egg | 22% of plate | 91 × 0.65 = 59 ml | 1.00 g/ml | 59 g |
| Avocado | 14% of plate | 58 × 1.1 = 64 ml | 0.70 g/ml | 45 g |
| Lemon wedge | 9% of plate | 37 × 1.5 = 56 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 34 g |
| Strawberries | 36% of bowl | 113 × 1.5 = 170 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 102 g |

The plate is approximately **71% covered**, and the bowl approximately **36% covered**. The yogurt is in a sealed retail cup, so I estimate **160 g** from its apparent package size rather than a visible food footprint.

**7 — Energy:** Toast ≈207 kcal; egg ≈116 kcal; avocado ≈72 kcal; lemon ≈10 kcal; strawberries ≈33 kcal; Greek yogurt ≈192 kcal.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **474 g of food and 630 kcal** is plausible for this tray. The lemon weight includes its rind; actual intake would be slightly lower if only its juice is used. Yogurt type and toast preparation are the largest energy uncertainties.
